_note: Error-correcting code models. Logical error per round: p_L = prefactor * (p_eff/threshold)^exponent(d). 'phys_per_logical' counts data + syndrome qubits of one logical patch. layout_overhead multiplies the patch count for routing space (lattice surgery). These are generic textbook-level fits, not a replacement for a circuit-level simulation. Codes added for the mid-2030s audit: 'cat_repetition' (phase-flip repetition code on bias-preserving cat qubits) and 'fusion_network' (fusion-based photonic computation). Both are COARSE ASSUMPTIONS, flagged in their entries. 'tile_formula' (physical qubits per logical qubit as a function of d) and 'exponent' are evaluated by qec.Code; 'bitflip_floor' adds an uncorrectable per-round floor (2d-1) * p_bitflip for biased-noise codes; 'default_decoder' is used when an architecture names none.

surface.label: Rotated surface code
surface.source: Fowler et al., PRA 86, 032324 (2012): p_L ~ 0.1 (p/p_th)^((d+1)/2), p_th ~ 1 %. 2d^2-1 qubits per rotated patch. CCZ factory footprint/time: order-of-magnitude from Gidney & Fowler (2019).

bivariate_bicycle.label: Bivariate-bicycle qLDPC ('gross' family)
bivariate_bicycle.source: Bravyi et al., Nature 627, 778 (2024): [[144,12,12]] gross code, 288 physical qubits for 12 logical. Threshold and prefactor are rough fits; needs long-range connectivity.

cat_repetition.label: Cat-qubit repetition code (phase-flip, bias-preserving CX)
cat_repetition.source: ASSUMPTION calibrated to published points: AWS Ocelot (Nature 2025) distance-5 repetition code uses 5 cat + 4 ancilla qubits and shows a flat total logical error of about 1.7 % per cycle between d=3 and d=5 (i.e. at threshold for its noise); Alice & Bob roadmap about 20 cat qubits per logical qubit at 1e-6 (company target). Threshold 2 %, prefactor 0.1, layout and factory numbers are order-of-magnitude choices; Gouzien et al. PRL 131, 040602 (2023) give 126,133 cat qubits for a 256-bit ECDLP in 9 h under optimistic hardware assumptions and should be used to check any change. Outer codes (LDPC-cat) are not modelled.

fusion_network.label: Fusion-based photonic network (surface-like fusion lattice)
fusion_network.source: ASSUMPTION. Fusion-based quantum computation (Bartolucci et al., Nature Commun. 14, 912, 2023) is not a surface code; here it is approximated by a surface-like scaling with an effective fusion-error threshold of 1 %, 6 d^2 resource-state generators per logical qubit (about 3x the surface code, covering multiplexing and heralding overhead) and the surface-code factory numbers. Replace with a fusion-lattice simulation before relying on any photonic qubit count.
